title: Turn workload demand into a bounded concurrency budget
description: Change the request rate, service time, workload shape, and worker limit. The model separates useful in-flight work from queue growth and CPU saturation.

profiles.label: I/O-bound requests
profiles.detail: Most time is spent waiting on a database, network, disk, or remote API.
profiles.guidance: Concurrency can exceed the CPU count, but every wait, queue, connection, and downstream dependency still needs a bound.

profiles.label: Mixed request work
profiles.detail: Each request alternates between CPU work and blocking I/O.
profiles.guidance: Size from measured CPU and wait time. A pool that hides I/O latency can still saturate CPU during bursts.

profiles.label: CPU-bound computation
profiles.detail: Most service time is runnable work such as parsing, compression, or cryptography.
profiles.guidance: Useful parallelism stays near available CPU. More goroutines mostly add queueing and scheduling overhead.

notice: This is a planning model, not a Go runtime benchmark. Real stack growth, allocation rate, scheduler behavior, downstream limits, and service-time tails must be measured under representative load.
